text:
ajay: quick thought — proposing a "soft-pin" routing primitive for model aliases. idea: route prefers pinned version but automatically falls back to any compatible variant when the pinned model is saturated or exceeding its quota. keeps rollouts gradual while avoiding hard outages.

maria: short q — how do we define "compatible"? semantic compatibility vs runtime (seq len / quantization).

ajay: both. compatibility is a two-part matcher: functional (model tag set: embeddings, chat-format, truncation-behavior) AND runtime constraints (max_seq_length, quantization flags, tokenizer family). config attached.

ajay: ```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "match": {"header.X-Customer":"acme-*", "method":"POST"},
  "model_selection": {
    "alias": "redwood-llm-large",
    "soft_pin": true,
    "canary_pct": 10,
    "compatibility_constraints": [
      "tokenizer_family:cl100k_base",
      "max_sequence_len:<=4096",
      "quantized:allowed"
    ],
    "fallback_policy": ["nearest_latency", "alias_weighted"]
  },
  "quotas": {"per_model_rps": 800, "route_burst": 2000}
}
```

kevin: important: header precedence — tenant header -> route explicit override -> alias default. if we let tenant headers override pins, ops will lose control. prefer route-level override only for safety.

taylor: console UX idea: show a tiny "exposure slider" next to alias that maps to canary_pct; also surface two panels when soft_pin=true: "pinned exposure" and "fallback volume". give links to traces where fallback decision happened.

maria: telemetry needs an explicit event for each decision: route_decision {reason: "soft_pin_fallback", chosen_model, candidate_list, latency_est, token_cost_est, telemetry_id}. otherwise we won't know if fallbacks drive customer-visible regressions.

ajay: agreed. propose these telemetry keys: route_decision.reason, route_decision.rank_score, route_decision.compat_checks, route_decision.fallback_used(true/false). tag with rollout_id when canary active.

kevin: also capture "quota_trigger" with counts so alerting can target model autoscale instead of the route. e.g., quota_trigger:{model_id, current_rps, threshold}.

ops-bot: deployment: soft-pin routing v1 deployed to staging at 2026-03-18T14:22Z by ajay.

maria: edge case: what if all compatible variants are _slower_ but cheaper? app owners might prefer latency SLOs — we need an explicit prefer_latency boolean or cost_sensitivity param on the route.

ajay: yep. extend fallback_policy to accept ordered tuples: ["prefer_latency", "alias_weighted"] vs ["prefer_cost"]. defaults to prefer_latency for customer-facing routes.

kevin: security note — model alias metadata contains tags which are user-controllable via model onboarding. need guardrails so compatibility tags can't be used to bypass safety pins. add an allowlist for tag-to-capability mapping.

taylor: console: telemetry drilldown should show a small flame-graph: upstream latency, model runtime, tokenization, and fallback penalty. show percentage of requests where soft-pin triggered. also allow filtering by rollout_id and tenant.

maria: API surface: add header X-Rd-Model-Steer: soft-pin to request when fallback occurs so client telemetry can correlate. set header only on responses we actually rerouted.

ajay: sample event emitted on fallback:
```json
{
  "evt": "route_decision",
  "ts": 2185554444,
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "tenant": "acme-123",
  "original_alias": "redwood-llm-large",
  "chosen_model": "rllm-large-v2-quant",
  "fallback_used": true,
  "reason": "pinned_exhausted_quota",
  "rollout_id": "canary-2026-03-17-a",
  "latency_ms": 72,
  "estimated_cost_tokens": 0.0032
}
```

kevin: love the event. make sure we don't log model weights or PII. redact tenant ids in public dashboards.

taylor: rollout UX question — when soft_pin=true and canary_pct>0, do we count fallback exposure against canary budget? i.e., if canary_pct=5 but fallback sends 10% of traffic to older variants, the effective canary exposure drops. need clarity.

ajay: we should separate two numbers: intended_canary_exposure (what console shows) and observed_canary_exposure (from telemetry). console should display both and offer auto-scale suggestions (increase canary or reduce fallback threshold).

maria: tests: add unit test for selector that enumerates candidates and fails if it selects an incompatible model. add fuzzy tests for heavy quota scenarios to ensure fallback triggers.

kevin: ops: for emergency rollback we need a single toggle on the route to disable soft_pin and force alias->pinned_model. console should mark that toggle with an audit entry.

ajay: plan for next week: (1) extend selector to accept compatibility matchers, (2) wire route_decision telemetry, (3) minimal console mock for exposure numbers + rollback toggle, (4) e2e tests for quota-trigger fallback.

taylor: sounds good. I'll prototype the console visuals — will post a screenshot in #eng-platform when ready.

ops-bot: reminder: RFC review for soft-pin routing scheduled 2026-03-20 15:00 UTC. Please comment on the RFC doc: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/soft-pin-routing

maria: commenting now on the doc with a couple of compatibility edge cases.

ajay: thanks all — will update the RFC with clarifications on telemetry and fallback scoring.

kevin: +1 on safety guardrails.

taylor: :thumbsup:
